Summary: Reusable software-development child process that breaks implementation into intake, architecture, optional solution setup, feature/function implementation, unit tests, and evidence handoff.
ValueStatement: Keeps a large implementation lane observable and manager-reportable by using small process steps plus nested setup and feature/function implementation subprocesses.
InterfaceContractSummary: The parent process supplies the change scope, repository target, architecture decision, and validation bar; this subprocess returns implementation and test evidence.
GovernanceNotes: Implementation work must remain split into typed, observable steps so blockers can be reported by managers without reading raw execution threads.
ChangeSummary: Adds the default atomic implementation subprocess used by the software-delivery process.
GovernancePolicySummary: A development slice cannot close until code change, tests, and validation evidence are durable and linked to the parent scope.
ConstitutionRuleSummary: The parent and child runs share process identity through explicit runtime relationships, not duplicated state or chat summaries.
OperatingModeSummary: Assisted execution with manager observation; process-level manager override can replace default HR matching for manager roles.
SimulationReadinessSummary: Small enough for real local validation while still exercising nested subprocess creation and child-run observation.
Metrics: Number of implementation slices completed without parent-step blockage.
Time spent blocked in scaffold, implementation, and validation phases.
Share of slices with test evidence attached before parent peer review.
Risks: Nested setup subprocess is used for an existing solution without explicit tailoring.
Code implementation expands beyond the approved slice boundary.
Validation evidence is missing or too broad to explain failures.
TailoringRules: Skip the generic .NET solution setup subprocess only when the repository already has a correct solution skeleton and the skip records explicit proof.
Use the app archetype, test framework, validation type, and product root from the current project structure or upstream architecture notes; escalate when those inputs conflict or are missing.

When the parent scope is a simple full app or one-shot full deliverable, keep every explicitly named core MVP behavior in this development slice and pass those criteria into the feature/function child subprocess. The MVP must not be scaffold-only, setup-only, naming-only, readiness-only, static-looking, or build-only proof; scaffolding is prerequisite evidence, not the accepted product behavior.

Split work into multiple instances only when the parent launch context supplies an explicit remaining-slice schedule. Without that schedule, do not defer a named core interaction, persistence requirement, calculation, search, dashboard, or recovery behavior to an unplanned later slice.
Keep parent approval and release gates in the parent process; this subprocess owns implementation proof only.

RoleUsages.Purpose: Report progress, blockers, and child subprocess status to the parent process.
RoleUsages.StaffingIntent: A manager-capable human or AI agent that can summarize high-volume execution data.

RoleUsages.Purpose: Confirm the slice fits the parent architecture and does not create hidden source-of-truth drift.
RoleUsages.StaffingIntent: Architecture reviewer for scoped design decisions and integration risks.

RoleUsages.Purpose: Implement the bounded change and maintain tests.
Confirm the implementation has focused tests and regression evidence.
RoleUsages.StaffingIntent: A reviewer capable of interpreting targeted test, build, and browser proof.

Steps.Title: Capture implementation slice boundary
Steps.Subtitle: Small enough to finish
Steps.Notes: Restate the parent scope as one bounded implementation slice with assumptions, exclusions, and validation hooks. If the parent asks for a simple full app or one-shot broad deliverable, retain every explicitly named core MVP behavior from upstream project-structure and architecture facts. The MVP must not be scaffold-only, setup-only, naming-only, readiness-only, static-looking, or build-only; it must include the complete recognizable interaction path, typed state transitions, and any named persistence, calculation, search, dashboard, or recovery behavior. Exclude only optional polish or a capability assigned to an explicit later-slice schedule. If project structure lists visual target assets, copy their ImageAsset node ids, media paths, and target-look notes into the slice acceptance criteria or validation hooks. Decide ProductTargetState from authoritative baseline provenance, not from a configured output-root alias or directory existence: select existing when current-run project structure, an upstream artifact, or a discovered DotNetProductBaselineContract with discoveryComplete true proves a baseline must be retained; select greenfield for a new deliverable with no such baseline. Copy the baseline contract's paths as the complete topology only when topologySampleComplete is true; otherwise use its counts and samples for bounded read-only topology discovery. Trust framework and test-project metadata only when metadataInspectionComplete is true. Not-found proves absence only when discoveryComplete is true. Partial, unavailable, duplicate-name, incomplete-sample, or incomplete-metadata baseline discovery is a topology warning, not permission to initialize over existing files. This is an intake step: do not run restore, build, test, app startup, or browser validation here.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Parent scope packet, repository context, and requested behavior.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Slice boundary with acceptance criteria, explicit ProductTargetState, setup needs, and excluded follow-up work.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Scope summary, assumptions, ProductTargetState with grounded evidence, setup/implementation handoff, and validation plan outline.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Slice manager can narrow execution scope but cannot silently discard parent acceptance criteria or downgrade a requested product to scaffold-only readiness.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Block when the slice cannot be made small enough for atomic validation, when the selected scope is only scaffold/setup/readiness work, or when the required product root, architecture, app archetype, validation boundary, or authoritative baseline evidence is contradictory or missing. Do not label a target existing merely because its configured directory or alias exists.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Rebind only to a manager-capable operator that can report to the parent run.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: Implementation slice scope packet
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable by parent peer review and future slices.
ArtifactExpectations.ValidationRequirementSummary: Must define acceptance criteria, exclusions, intended product root, setup needs, validation hooks, and exactly one ProductTargetState: greenfield or existing; grounded target root; and current-run evidence. Greenfield means no authoritative product baseline must be preserved even when a directory or preliminary files exist. Existing means an authoritative baseline must be retained and modified and must cite the authoritative baseline topology or artifact. A target alias, configured output root, or directory existence alone is not existing-baseline evidence. When the request is for a new deliverable and no baseline is identified, record greenfield.

InstructionFragments.Title: Product target state decision
InstructionFragments.Content: ProductTargetState is a semantic baseline-provenance decision, not a filesystem classification. Select existing when current-run project structure, an upstream artifact, or a runtime-owned DotNetProductBaselineContract with status discovered and discoveryComplete true proves an authoritative baseline must be retained. Copy the contract paths as complete topology only when topologySampleComplete is true; otherwise the arrays are samples and bounded read-only discovery must resolve the exact topology. Trust framework and test-project metadata only when metadataInspectionComplete is true. Treat not-found as absence evidence only when discoveryComplete is true. A configured target alias, output root, or directory existence is not enough. A partial, unavailable, duplicate-name, incomplete-sample, or incomplete-metadata baseline contract is explicit topology-warning evidence and must not be treated as greenfield permission. When the requested deliverable is new and no authoritative baseline is identified, select greenfield even if the target directory already exists; cite the new-deliverable input and the absence of baseline evidence. If evidence conflicts, return Blocked with the exact contradiction instead of guessing.

Steps.Title: Check architecture and source-of-truth impact
Steps.Subtitle: No hidden ownership drift
Steps.Notes: Confirm canonical models, integration boundaries, persistence ownership, and UI/application/domain responsibilities before code starts. Read the upstream ProductTargetState before producing a solution context: greenfield requires initialize and an explicit initialization plan; existing requires verify-existing and read-only proof of the exact current topology. A discovered DotNetProductBaselineContract with discoveryComplete true is runtime-owned current-run evidence that a baseline exists. Preserve its listed relative paths as the complete topology only when topologySampleComplete is true; otherwise complete bounded read-only topology discovery from its counts and samples. Trust framework and test-project metadata only when metadataInspectionComplete is true. Not-found proves absence only when discoveryComplete is true. Partial, unavailable, duplicate-name, incomplete-sample, or incomplete-metadata discovery requires bounded clarification. ProductTargetFilesystemState is physical observation only and does not override target intent. This architecture step must not run restore, build, test, app startup, or browser proof; block on a concrete target-state contradiction instead of guessing or retrying the same classification.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Slice scope packet including ProductTargetState and parent architecture notes.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Architecture decision record or explicit no-ADR rationale plus a solution context whose provisioning mode agrees with ProductTargetState.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Touched boundaries, source-of-truth decision, and risk notes.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Slice architect can require split or escalation when ownership boundaries are unclear.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Block on canonical model ambiguity, persistence ownership conflict, unsafe cross-layer leakage, contradictory project-structure requirements, or artifact recovery when required architecture evidence is missing or invalid before branch routing. Do not block only because a greenfield product root does not exist yet.

InstructionFragments.Title: .NET solution-context authoring contract
InstructionFragments.Content: This step has two required outputs in the same primary managed Markdown artifact: the architecture decision narrative and one machine-readable .NET solution context. Keep the narrative, then include exactly one fenced `json` block in the entire artifact; do not use a second `json` block for examples, notes, or diagnostics. That one JSON object must declare `schema` exactly `dotnet.solution-context/v1`, `provisioningMode`, `solution.file`, non-empty `requiredProjectFiles`, and optional `testProjectFiles`, using only bare ProductRoot-relative paths. The runtime derives the same-name `.sln` and `.slnx` alternatives from `solution.file`; omit optional `solution.candidateFiles` unless the accepted architecture genuinely declares additional non-equivalent solution candidates. For ProductTargetState greenfield, set `provisioningMode` to `initialize` and include an `initialization` object with `solutionName`, `application` (name, directory, file, template, templateOptions, optional archetype), `tests` (name, directory, file, template, frameworkPreference), and `targetFramework`. For existing, set `provisioningMode` to `verify-existing`, include only topology proved by current read-only evidence, and omit `initialization`. application.templateOptions represents optional dotnet new flags only: use [] when none is required, and make every non-empty item one --prefixed option flag rather than a feature label, template name, archetype, or bare value. Before the first write, perform one whole-payload type-and-completeness self-check: the root, `solution`, and `initialization` (when required) are JSON objects; `requiredProjectFiles`, optional `testProjectFiles`, optional `solution.candidateFiles`, and `application.templateOptions` are JSON arrays; every required nested object and scalar is present for the selected provisioning mode; and the artifact contains exactly one fenced `json` block. Do not write a partial payload and rely on a later retry to discover the next missing field. Narrative alone is not a substitute for this payload, and a schema-looking second artifact or sibling file does not satisfy the declared output.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Rebind only to an architect-capable reviewer.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: Slice architecture decision record
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable by implementation, peer review, and parent release approval.
ArtifactExpectations.ValidationRequirementSummary: Must name source-of-truth ownership and cross-layer impact.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: .NET solution context
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable by the bounded setup subprocess, implementation, repair, and validation without inferring product topology.
ArtifactExpectations.ValidationRequirementSummary: Must contain exactly one fenced json block with schema dotnet.solution-context/v1, explicit provisioningMode, solution.file, explicit requiredProjectFiles, optional testProjectFiles, and ProductRoot-relative paths. Runtime derives same-name .sln and .slnx alternatives; solution.candidateFiles is only for additional non-equivalent candidates. Before writing, self-check the entire payload: root, solution, and required initialization are objects; project/candidate/template-option collections are arrays; every non-empty application.templateOptions item is one --prefixed option flag; and every nested required value for the selected mode is present. Greenfield ProductTargetState requires initialize with a separate complete initialization plan; existing ProductTargetState requires verify-existing with read-only grounded topology. Never use native absolute paths, external-target aliases, ProductRoot prefixes, or managed-artifact paths. Verify-existing must omit initialization and report contradictions rather than inventing topology.

Steps.Title: Establish solution baseline subprocess
Steps.Subtitle: Initialize or verify declared context
Steps.Notes: Launch the isolated .NET solution baseline subprocess from the explicit bound solution context. An initialize context may create only its declared baseline; a verify-existing context is read-only and must not infer templates, names, framework, test framework, layout, or project relationships from prose. Accept either setup-handoff or setup-handoff-after-repair as valid baseline proof; treat setup-repair-escalation as no-go blocker evidence.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Slice scope, architecture decision, and typed solution context.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Observed child run that initializes a declared baseline or verifies an explicit existing solution context.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Child run status, declared-context verification or initialization proof, setup-handoff or setup-handoff-after-repair packet, and setup-repair-escalation no-go evidence when present.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: The child follows the explicit provisioningMode; it does not infer whether to initialize or verify from directory contents or prose.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Block the slice when the child baseline run blocks, fails, reports setup-repair-escalation, or lacks setup-handoff/setup-handoff-after-repair evidence.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Rebind only to a .NET-capable implementer that can coordinate setup evidence and child run output.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: Solution baseline evidence
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable by implementation and validation steps.
ArtifactExpectations.ValidationRequirementSummary: Must point to the observed child run and its declared-context initialization or read-only verification proof. setup-repair-escalation is blocker evidence, not accepted baseline proof.

Steps.Title: Implement bounded code change through subprocess
Steps.Subtitle: Observed feature run
Steps.Notes: Launch the feature/function implementation subprocess for the bounded behavior in this slice. First call project_structure_process_subprocess_launch with definitionKey dotnet-feature-function-implementation; do not wait silently or return Blocked before attempting that child launch unless mandatory launch inputs are missing. Before launch, carry forward the concrete MVP behavior, product root, app archetype, setup handoff, acceptance criteria, validation hooks, and exclusions from the slice artifacts so the child receives one implementable request. When the slice scope includes visual target ImageAsset ids or media paths, include them in the child request and require the visible implementation to use those assets as the design target. Do not launch this child when the slice scope only asks for scaffold readiness, solution setup, naming, or generic app-shell existence. If the launch response includes ParentDeferredOutcomeJson, submit that parent outcome exactly: active child runs defer the parent, completed child runs complete the parent from child evidence, and stopped child runs propagate their concrete blocker. Observe the child run status, change-set artifact, validation evidence, accepted handoff artifacts, repair escalation artifacts, blockers, and manager-directed rework without duplicating child runtime state in this parent step.

AcceptedChildOutputs.ArtifactTitle: Feature implementation handoff packet after repair

NoGoChildOutputs.ArtifactTitle: Feature repair escalation packet for manager-assisted repair
Feature repair recheck no-go evidence for manager-assisted repair

Steps.InputContractSummary: Slice scope, architecture decision, solution skeleton evidence, and one bounded feature or function request derived from the parent scope when needed.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Observed child run that returns a reviewable code change, focused validation evidence, blockers, and residual risks.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Child run status, implementation change set, validation evidence, accepted handoff evidence, repair escalation evidence, manager rework directives, and unresolved blockers.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Implementation engineer can request targeted child-run repair but cannot widen behavior beyond the slice boundary.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Block the slice when the child implementation run blocks or fails without a typed output. A completed feature-repair-escalation packet is an explicit no-go disposition, not accepted implementation proof: route it to the manager-assisted repair branch with its typed evidence.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Rebind only to a .NET-capable implementer that can observe child implementation runs and request targeted rework.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: Slice implementation change set
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable by tests, peer review, and parent QA.
ArtifactExpectations.ValidationRequirementSummary: Must record the observed child implementation run, runtime-accepted child disposition, selected parent branch, and exact typed handoff ref from feature-handoff or feature-handoff-after-repair, and must preserve the exact selected child artifact payload inside the runtime-owned hash-verified envelope. The typed accepted/no-go disposition and parent branch remain canonical; consumers must not re-decide them from prose or require a separate agent-authored restatement of the preserved payload. Detailed product and validation claims remain subject to independent downstream readback and proof. A feature-repair-escalation packet is blocker evidence, not accepted implementation proof.

BranchOutcomes.Title: Implementation child accepted
BranchOutcomes.Description: The child returned an accepted feature handoff that can proceed to slice validation.

BranchOutcomes.Title: Implementation child requires manager-assisted repair
BranchOutcomes.Description: The child returned typed no-go evidence; preserve it and start the bounded manager-assisted repair path.

Steps.Title: Validate tests and targeted proof
Steps.Subtitle: Validation commands before handoff
Steps.Notes: Validate the declared product behavior with current-run restore, build, and test evidence. Read the required typed dotnet-solution-context artifact first for the declared solution and test targets; its declared paths are authoritative. If it is unavailable, use grounded product-root discovery without constructing conventional names or layouts. Never treat a missing guessed target as a product defect. The runtime-synthesized implementation-ready coordinator outcome is the canonical accepted-child provenance and carries the exact hash-verified selected child payload; use that authenticated payload as context, but do not re-decide the typed bridge from prose or require a separate agent-authored restatement. Run restore before build or test when assets are stale. Do not mutate code or tests in this QA step; route only a concrete product, test, or focused-proof criterion to the repair branch.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Authoritative slice scope packet, implementation change set, and slice architecture decision; every named core criterion remains in scope until directly proved.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Test and validation evidence review tied to the implemented behavior, with explicit slice-accepted or slice-repair-required branch.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Current-run restore/build/test commands, exit codes, warnings, executed tests, typed runtime-synthesized coordinator provenance, explicit assessment of whether product proof satisfies acceptance criteria, and a concrete product/test/proof repair target packet whenever repair is selected. Live runtime screenshots are owned by root runtime-command and screenshot writeback steps.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Validation owner can accept evidence or require focused implementation rework when proof or tests do not match acceptance criteria, but cannot mutate product files.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Select slice-repair-required on missing tests, failing build, failing focused validation, validation too broad to diagnose failures, or invalid product evidence that still has a repair route. A runtime-synthesized implementation-ready coordinator with accepted disposition, an exact typed child evidence ref, and the hash-verified selected child payload already proves the child bridge; absence of a separate agent-authored restatement is not a product repair target. Block only when the environment, permissions, validation tooling, or process contract prevents validation or repair routing.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Rebind only to a reviewer capable of evaluating targeted test evidence.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: Slice test evidence
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable by parent QA and release approval.
ArtifactExpectations.ValidationRequirementSummary: Must include current-run restore/build/test commands, exit codes, executed-test counts when a test project exists or tests are expected, proof tied to acceptance criteria, and review of typed runtime-synthesized coordinator provenance, its exact hash-verified selected child payload, plus product readback. If tests or product acceptance evidence are missing or inadequate, the artifact must route repair to implementation with an exact product/test/proof repair target packet instead of recording QA-authored product changes or generic residual risk. Do not route product repair because a separate agent-authored restatement is absent from an accepted runtime coordinator artifact. Live browser proof belongs to root runtime-command and screenshot writeback steps.

BranchOutcomes.Title: Slice accepted
BranchOutcomes.Description: Slice validation evidence is sufficient for parent handoff.

BranchOutcomes.Title: Slice repair required
BranchOutcomes.Description: Slice validation found missing tests, failed product proof, or another concrete product issue requiring bounded implementation repair.

Steps.Subtitle: Parent-ready accepted evidence

Steps.InputContractSummary: Scope, architecture, accepted change set, and accepted test evidence.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Parent-ready implementation handoff with blockers and residual risks.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Implementation summary, validation result, open issues, and explicit next action.

Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Do not close on the initial path when validation selected repair-required, tests fail, blockers remain untriaged, or the parent cannot determine next action.

Steps.Title: Run manager-assisted repair for child no-go
Steps.Subtitle: Diagnose before repeating implementation
Steps.Notes: Launch and observe the dotnet-quality-repair subprocess when the initial feature child returned typed no-go evidence. This is not a blind retry: the child no-go packet, scope, architecture decision, and setup evidence define the repair target. First call project_structure_process_subprocess_launch with definitionKey dotnet-quality-repair. If the launch response includes ParentDeferredOutcomeJson, submit that parent outcome exactly so the runtime resumes this coordinator from the child result. The repair child owns diagnosis, exactly three bounded mutation opportunities, and independent validation after each opportunity. This parent step only preserves the no-go evidence and materializes accepted repair handoff; it must not mutate the product or reinterpret quality-repair-no-go as success.
Steps.SubprocessDefinitionSnapshotName: .NET quality repair for initial feature child no-go

AcceptedChildOutputs.ArtifactTitle: .NET quality repair handoff after final specialist repair

Steps.InputContractSummary: Authoritative slice scope, architecture decision, setup evidence, and typed initial feature-child no-go evidence.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Accepted manager-assisted repair change set with independent validation, or an explicit quality-repair no-go for manager attention.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Child no-go packet, diagnosis and mutation chain, current independent validation, and accepted or terminal no-go quality-repair handoff.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: The delivery manager sequences the bounded repair child; the child retains mutation and independent-validation separation across all three opportunities.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Block only when the quality-repair child blocks, fails, or returns quality-repair-no-go. Do not restart the same feature strategy without the child diagnosis changing the repair plan.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Rebind only to a manager-capable operator that can preserve no-go evidence and repair scope.
Review whether the repair target follows the failed evidence rather than repeating the prior attempt.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: Initial manager-assisted repair change set
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable by parent QA, release approval, and later defect analysis.
ArtifactExpectations.ValidationRequirementSummary: Must point to accepted dotnet-quality-repair handoff with diagnosis, changed surfaces, current validation, and coverage of the original slice criteria.

Steps.Title: Hand off initial manager-repaired slice
Steps.Subtitle: Parent-ready repair evidence
Steps.Notes: Produce this parent-ready handoff only after initial-manager-assisted-repair returned accepted quality-repair evidence. Reconcile that evidence with every criterion in the authoritative slice scope. Do not present a child no-go, unresolved criterion, or an unproved assertion as accepted.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Authoritative scope, initial child no-go evidence, and accepted manager-assisted repair change set.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Parent-ready implementation handoff after manager-assisted recovery of initial child no-go.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: No-go diagnosis, repaired surfaces, independent validation, criterion coverage, residual risks, and parent next action.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: The delivery manager can close only from accepted repair evidence and full criterion coverage.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Do not close when accepted quality-repair handoff is missing, a core criterion remains unresolved, or the repair child returned no-go.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Rebind only to a manager-capable operator that can reconcile repair evidence with the parent scope.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: Implementation slice handoff after initial manager-assisted repair
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable by parent peer review, QA, and release approval.
ArtifactExpectations.ValidationRequirementSummary: Must include accepted manager-assisted repair evidence, independent validation, criterion-by-criterion coverage, unresolved risks, and recommended parent action.

Steps.Title: Repair slice findings through subprocess
Steps.Subtitle: Bounded repair child run
Steps.Notes: Launch a feature/function implementation subprocess for the concrete slice validation findings. First call project_structure_process_subprocess_launch with definitionKey dotnet-feature-function-implementation; do not wait silently or return Blocked before attempting that child launch unless mandatory repair-launch inputs are missing. Carry forward the exact repair target packet from add-tests-and-proof, including failed acceptance criteria, failing command or browser metrics, child run id, child step artifact refs, product root, app archetype, setup handoff, accepted slice boundary, exclusions, and the smallest proof that would close the defect. Do not ask the child subprocess to select a fresh MVP behavior; this is a repair launch and the child feature scope must inherit the repair target as mandatory acceptance criteria. If the launch response includes ParentDeferredOutcomeJson, submit that parent outcome exactly: active child runs defer the parent, completed child runs complete the parent from child evidence, and stopped child runs propagate their concrete blocker. The child repair run must return accepted handoff evidence or explicit repair escalation evidence.

AcceptedChildOutputs.ArtifactTitle: Feature implementation handoff packet after repair

Steps.InputContractSummary: Authoritative slice scope packet plus the exact validation failure, repair target packet, implementation change set, architecture decision, and bounded repair request; the latest defect must not narrow away other core criteria.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Observed child repair run with change set, validation proof, accepted handoff, or reviewable repair escalation evidence for the parent recheck.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Child repair run status, changed files, validation evidence, accepted handoff evidence, repair escalation evidence, and unresolved blockers.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Implementation engineer can request bounded repair but cannot widen the slice beyond the parent-approved boundary.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Block when the child repair run itself blocks or fails. Materialize a completed child repair-escalation packet for parent recheck and manager-assisted recovery; do not treat that packet as accepted product proof.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: Slice repair change set
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable by repaired slice recheck, parent QA, and release approval.

A feature-repair-escalation packet is blocker evidence, not accepted repair proof.

Steps.Title: Recheck slice proof after repair
Steps.Subtitle: Repaired validation commands
Steps.Notes: Revalidate the original repair target with current-run restore, build, and test evidence. Read the required typed dotnet-solution-context artifact first for the declared solution and test targets; its declared paths are authoritative. If it is unavailable, use grounded product-root discovery without constructing conventional names or layouts. Never treat a missing guessed target as a product defect. Run restore before build or test when assets are stale. Do not mutate code or tests in this QA recheck; escalate only a concrete unresolved criterion or an execution boundary.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Authoritative slice scope packet, original validation failure, repair child evidence, and architecture decision; recheck must account for every original core criterion.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Repaired slice validation evidence with explicit slice-accepted or slice-repair-escalation branch.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Current-run restore/build/test commands, exit codes, warnings, executed tests, current-run repair coordinator evidence, original repair target before/after assessment, and unresolved gaps after repair. Live runtime/browser proof belongs to root runtime-command and screenshot writeback steps.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Validation owner can accept repaired evidence or escalate unresolved repair findings; QA still cannot mutate product files.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Select slice-repair-escalation when proof remains failing, missing, detached, or unmapped after repair. Block only when an environment, permission, or process-contract issue prevents recheck execution.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Rebind only to a reviewer capable of evaluating targeted repaired test evidence.
Manager reviews unresolved repaired findings before parent escalation.

ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable by parent QA and release approval.
ArtifactExpectations.ValidationRequirementSummary: Must include current-run restore/build/test commands, exit codes, executed-test counts when a test project exists or tests are expected, proof tied to acceptance criteria, review of current-run repair coordinator evidence and repair coverage, and unresolved gaps after repair.

Steps.Title: Prepare manager-assisted slice repair
Steps.Subtitle: Manager diagnosis handoff
Steps.Notes: Record unresolved repaired validation findings as a manager diagnosis input. The absence of an accepted child handoff is a routing symptom, not itself a repair target, and the downstream quality-repair subprocess cannot manufacture a child handoff. Preserve the authoritative slice scope, trace why the child withheld acceptance back to the unresolved product behavior or executable proof, distinguish repeated implementation strategy from the acceptance contract, and identify the owning source, failed proof, and smallest mutation-plus-validation loop. Green restore/build/test receipts do not make a presentational shell or missing original workflow proof-only. This artifact is reviewable recovery evidence, not a parent no-go or accepted product proof.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Authoritative slice scope, original validation failure, repair child run evidence, and failed repaired recheck evidence.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Manager repair diagnosis packet with unresolved defects, proof gaps, repeated-strategy analysis, and a bounded mutation-plus-validation target.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Unresolved blocker list, failing proof references, attempted repair, authoritative acceptance criteria, owning source, and recommended manager-assisted repair action.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Slice manager can sequence one diagnosis-guided quality repair subprocess but cannot present unresolved findings as accepted.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Do not continue to parent-ready accepted handoff while repaired validation remains unresolved; prepare the bounded manager-assisted repair unless a genuine permission, environment, or contradictory-requirement blocker prevents it.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Rebind only to a manager-capable operator that can report no-go evidence to the parent run.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: Slice repair escalation packet
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable by parent peer review, incident review, and future repair planning.
ArtifactExpectations.ValidationRequirementSummary: Must summarize unresolved findings, attempted repair, failing proof, no-go rationale, and required next scope.

Steps.Title: Run manager-assisted quality repair
Steps.Subtitle: Diagnosis, three bounded repair lanes, and independent validation
Steps.Notes: Launch and observe the dotnet-quality-repair subprocess for the unresolved slice findings. First call project_structure_process_subprocess_launch with definitionKey dotnet-quality-repair. Do not wait silently, write a progress artifact, or create another child while one is active. If the launch response includes ParentDeferredOutcomeJson, submit that parent outcome exactly so the runtime resumes this step from the child result. The child receives the authoritative slice scope, both validation packets, the failed repair evidence, and the manager diagnosis. It owns diagnosis, exactly three bounded mutation opportunities with independent validation, and accepted or terminal no-go handoff. This parent step only coordinates the child and materializes accepted handoff evidence; it must not mutate the product or reinterpret a quality-repair-no-go packet as success.
Steps.SubprocessDefinitionSnapshotName: .NET quality repair with three bounded repair lanes

AcceptedChildOutputs.ArtifactTitle: .NET quality repair handoff after final specialist repair

Steps.InputContractSummary: Authoritative slice scope, original and repaired validation failures, failed child repair evidence, and manager diagnosis; repair action may narrow but acceptance scope may not.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Accepted manager-assisted repair change set after any bounded child lane, or explicit terminal child no-go.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Child status, diagnosis and mutation chain, restore/build/test proof, owning-source readback, conditional runtime proof, and accepted or terminal no-go handoff.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Delivery manager owns repair sequencing; implementation and independent validation remain separate child roles.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Block only when the child blocks, fails, or returns quality-repair-no-go after all three bounded mutation opportunities. Do not relaunch the same failed feature-repair strategy.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Manager-assisted repair observation remains with a manager-capable role.
Engineering reviews the bounded repair scope without replacing independent child validation.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: Manager-assisted slice repair change set
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable by parent QA, release approval, and later defect analysis.
ArtifactExpectations.ValidationRequirementSummary: Must point to an accepted dotnet-quality-repair child handoff with diagnosis, changed files, current-execution validation, and confirmation that the original slice criteria remain covered.

Steps.Title: Hand off manager-repaired implementation slice
Steps.Subtitle: Parent-ready manager-assisted evidence
Steps.Notes: Produce the parent-ready handoff only after the manager-assisted quality repair subprocess returned accepted handoff evidence. Reconcile that evidence with every criterion in the authoritative slice scope and state the owning production surface and proof for each core behavior. Do not present a quality-repair-no-go or unresolved criterion as accepted.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Authoritative slice scope, manager diagnosis, and accepted manager-assisted repair change set with independent validation.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Parent-ready implementation handoff after manager-assisted repair with criterion coverage and residual risks.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Manager diagnosis, changed product surfaces, independent validation, bughunt evidence when used, criterion coverage, open risks, and explicit parent next action.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Delivery manager can close only from accepted manager-assisted repair evidence and full criterion coverage.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Do not close when accepted child handoff is missing, any authoritative core criterion remains unresolved, or the child returned no-go.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Rebind only to a manager-capable operator that can reconcile accepted repair evidence with the parent scope.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: Implementation slice handoff after manager-assisted repair
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable by parent peer review, QA, and release approval.
ArtifactExpectations.ValidationRequirementSummary: Must include accepted manager-assisted repair evidence, independent validation, criterion-by-criterion scope coverage, unresolved risks, and recommended parent action.
